input.short_description: Efficiently reload historical data into your destinations to backfill gaps or recover from issues.
input.body:
Backfill historical data

When you need to reload historical data into your destinations, a backfill pipeline lets you efficiently process past events without affecting your live pipeline.

Use cases

  • Recovering from a failed connector or destination issue
  • Loading historical data after adding a new destination
  • Correcting transformed data with an updated transformation logic
  • Populating a new data warehouse or analytics system

Best practices

When backfilling data:

  • Create a dedicated backfill pipeline to avoid impacting live traffic
  • Use time-range filtering to process data in batches
  • Monitor the backfill progress and watch for errors
  • Test with a small date range before running the full backfill

input.short_description: Send data from a single source to multiple destinations with transformation per destination.
input.body:
Fan-out to multiple destinations

A fan-out pattern lets you send events from a single source to multiple destinations, with destination-specific transformations applied to each branch.

Use cases

  • Sending to both a data warehouse and a real-time analytics platform
  • Splitting events between a primary and backup destination
  • Routing different event types to different systems
  • Replicating data across multiple regions or environments

Benefits

  • Single source of truth for data ingestion
  • Consistent transformation logic across branches
  • Simplified error handling and monitoring
  • Easy to add or remove destinations without restructuring
